projects.name: ONE UNEP Plastic Project on Accelerating a Global Circular Plastic Economy to Reduce Plastic Pollution and its Impacts
projects.description: The project applies a programmatic approach to contribute to the achievement of the UNEP MTS Direct Outcome 3.2 “Global Plastic Pollution is reduced” by 2027, through systems and circular solutions adopted by governments, businesses, financial institutions, and individuals, with a long-term vision to end plastic pollution by 2040.
projects.outcome: Output 4.3.1 Enhanced coordination and efficient implementation of sustainable waste management/beneficiation programmes

framework.name: Strategic Priority 1: Inclusive, just and sustainable economic growth

children.name: Outcome 1.1 By 2025, all people in South Africa, particularly women, youth and other marginalized groups, benefit justly from decent work and other social and economic opportunities

Output 1.1.1: Productive economic resources, markets, and opportunities enabled to increase equitable access by women, youth and other marginalized groups gender cohorts through policy advocacy, and capacity development.

Output 1.1.2: Policy environment and national capacity enhanced to expand social protection coverage including through strengthened resilience to socio-economic crises and disasters, targeting children, women, youth and other marginalized gender cohorts

Output 1.1.3: Entrepreneurship and skills development programmes strengthened, targeting in particular youth, women, and other marginalized gender cohorts including with a focus on digital and green technological innovations
Outcome 1.2: By 2025, South Africa´s primary, secondary and tertiary sectors are more productive, diversified, sustainable and employment-intensive

Output 1.2.1: Institutional capacities of key public and private sectors improved to deliver inclusive green economy investment policies, and labour market interventions that deliver decent employment, productivity, and resilient livelihoods to benefit marginalized gender cohorts, children, women, youth, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers and persons with disability

Output 1.2.2:  Policy and regulatory environment, as well as institutional mechanisms/ capacities at national and subnational level developed and implemented to unlock value chains in catalytic sectors (including the informal sector)

framework.name: Strategic Priority 2: Human capital and social transformation

children.name: Outcome 2.1:  By 2025, all people in South Africa, especially women and girls, vulnerable and marginalized populations, have protection from violence and discrimination and enjoy improved human rights and social cohesion
2.1.2: Enhanced coordination and strengthened capacity of all national and local systems to prevent and respond to violence and victims /survivors of violence

2.1.3:  Strengthen capacity of relevant duty bearers and rights holders on human rights-based approach at all levels, starting with families, stakeholders in communities, representatives of line departments, traditional and religious leaders

Output 2.1.1:  Policy, legislation and advocacy support to prevent and address the persistent discriminatory partiarchial social norms and stigma through education, awareness raising and behavioral change initiatives
Outcome 2.2:  By 2025, all people in South Africa, particularly vulnerable and marginalized populations, enjoy improved health, nutrition and well-being
Output 2.2.1: Strengthened resilient and inclusive, people- centred health systems and implementation of the National Health Insurance towards achieving Universal Health Coverage

Output 2.2.2: Strengthened capacities of health and related sectors to enable improved access to quality preventive, promotive, treatment and support services at the national and subnational levels, to address the quadruple burden of diseases  (Communicable Diseases; Noncommunicable Diseases; Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, Adolescent health and Nutrition; Violence and Injuries) and risk factors
Output 2.2.3: Strengthened health security to rapidly identify and respond to public health emergencies
Outcome 2.3:  By 2025, all children and young people in South Africa have equitable access to quality education relevant to a changing society

Output 2.3.1 National and subnational institutions and systems have strengthened capacities to plan, implement and monitor quality early learning programmes, policies and strategies for children under 6 years old

Output 2.3.2 National and subnational education systems have enhanced capacities to deliver inclusive, equitable and quality basic education for learners in the foundation, intermediate and senior phases with specific attention to reading, science, technology, engineering and math
Output 2.3.3 Adolescent girls and boys are capacitated, empowered, civically engaged and equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills as active citizens effectively transitioning to adulthood

framework.name: Strategic Priority 3: Effective, efficient and transformative governance

children.name: Outcome 3.1: By 2025, women and marginalized groups participate meaningfully in decision making processes and access justice

Output 3.1.1 : Strengthened capacity of government as duty bearers to enhance democratic, decision-making and development processes , demonstrated through greater meaningful participation of rights holders including marginalized groups at risk of being left behind.
Output 3.1.2: Increased capacity of oversight bodies and rights holders to effectively access justice and claim their rights.
Outcome 3.2: By 2025, state institutions deliver effective public services to all and oversight bodies are strengthened
Output 3.2.1: Strengthened accountability systems to promote ethical behaviour and intergrity  in the private and public sectors

Output 3.2.2: Increased capacity of government and state institutions as duty bearers to comply with its international human rights obligations and of key stakeholders including the SAHRC and other institutions supporting democracy and civil society organisations to effectively engage with the UN human rights mechanisms
Output 3.2.3: Strengthened capacity of state to deliver integrated and equitable services and fulfil human rights for all.

framework.name: Strategic Priority 4: Climate resilience and sustainably managed natural resources

children.name: Outcome 4.3: By 2025, South Africa is on course to a pollution/waste free environment, where the communities and the economy are optimally benefiting from waste
Output 4.3.1 Enhanced coordination and efficient implementation of sustainable waste management/beneficiation programmes
Outcome 4.1: By 2025, South Africa is on a just transition to a low-carbon society and vulnerable and marginalized communities adapt and are more resilient to adverse effects of climate change
Output 4.1.1 Institutional capacities of National and sub-national Government strengthened to facilitate a Just Transition to a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy/society
Output 4.1.2 Climate Change Adaptation Capacity of National, sub-national Government and communities strengthened for household food and nutrition, water and energy security
Outcome 4.2: By 2025, natural resources are managed and utilized sustainably for improved livelihoods, health and well-being of vulnerable communities
Output 4.2.1 Strenghtened capacity of national and sub-national institutions to sustainably and efficiently manage Natural Resources

Output 4.2.2 Strengthened capacity of national and sub-national institutions to enable vulnerable, marginalised communities and indigenous people to equitably access and justly benefit from Natural Resources
